title: A día de hoy: hablar de la situación actual

sections.content: A día de hoy (as of today, to this day) anchors a statement firmly in the present, often to contrast it with an earlier historical situation -- useful for closing a historical narrative by noting what still holds true, or what has changed, up to now. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: A día de hoy, tras la anulación de estas leyes de amnistía, cientos de nuevos juicios se han reabierto en Argentina.
items.english: As of today, following the annulment of these amnesty laws, hundreds of new trials have reopened in Argentina.

items.spanish: En Chile, la ley de amnistía de 1978 sigue generando, a día de hoy, un intenso debate legal y político.
items.english: In Chile, the 1978 amnesty law is still generating, to this day, intense legal and political debate.

items.spanish: A día de hoy, la tensión entre memoria, justicia y reconciliación sigue sin resolverse completamente.
items.english: As of today, the tension between memory, justice and reconciliation still hasn't been fully resolved.

items.spanish: A día de hoy, ese antiguo centro de detención es un sitio de memoria abierto al público.
items.english: As of today, that former detention center is a memory site open to the public.

sections.content: A día de hoy usually pairs with the present perfect (se han reabierto) or the simple present (sigue generando) -- it's about what's still true now, so it rarely appears with a past tense on its own.
